items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: who was part of the Les Six, you know, the Darius Milhaud and

ctx.x: Yeah. I have an excerpt where Paul Robeson connects an African melody that predated Bach. An East African chorale forum he describes it, then syncs and eleventh century Czechoslovakian — it sounds like one melody. He seamlessly weaves it and this is predated Bach. And the reason why I said Bach is because when I studied different composers that have train themes there was a connection not only of the folk forms of those countries where those composers came from, but also there was a connection with the music of…

Erik Satie. And he wrote a piece in 1923 or 1924 called “Pacific 231.” And he recognized Bach as a major influence in the work. The music itself rates more of the technology — 231 is in reference to the axle design of the train. And to me that’s maybe related to the Italian futuristic movement, the art movement that had, you know, celebrated technology. And later on we see, in the 1930’s, the artist Diego Rivera, who painted those amazing Detroit industry murals celebrating not only technology but also the worker…
